tools.source: interlock host tools py-thousands --role worker --host claude-code

sessions.final_text:
`balances` and `settle` now print amounts with thousands separators, so `settle` shows `-121,810.78` style values (for example `Bea -> Ann  121,810.78` on `examples/big.csv`).

I added an opt-in `thousands` parameter to `format_cents` in `tally/money.py`, and `tally/report.py` passes it for both commands. It defaults to off, so the CSV export, which also uses `format_cents`, is unchanged.

`interlock check run` passed for `balances` (`checks/thousands.sh`) and `regression` (19 unit tests). I ran `settle` on `examples/big.csv` by hand to confirm its output. I recorded claims for all three criteria. I didn't add a unit test or touch the README.

- **balances**: Holds (observed). `interlock check run --criterion balances` passed on tree 5c1935c, and `balances` on `examples/big.csv` printed `-121,810.78`.
- **spec**: Holds (observed). `settle` printed `121,810.78` and `balances` printed `-121,810.78`. `format_cents` takes an opt-in `thousands` flag, so the CSV export in `tally/export.py` still prints plain amounts. Only `tally/money.py` and `tally/report.py` changed, which is inside the allowed scope.
- **regression**: Holds (tested). The 19 unit tests passed in interlock's run on this tree. The worker added no new unit test for the separators, so that check only shows nothing broke.

checks_run: git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}; git diff 290aa6f --stat; interlock check run --criterion balances; interlock check run --criterion regression; python3 -m tally settle examples/big.csv; python3 -m tally balances examples/big.csv; git diff 290aa6f -- tally; ls examples

interlock assess add --criterion balances --strength observed --ref "interlock check run --criterion balances" --note "Check passed on tree 5c1935c; balances output shows -121,810.78"
interlock assess add --criterion spec --strength observed --ref "python3 -m tally settle/balances examples/big.csv; git diff 290aa6f -- tally" --note "settle prints 121,810.78, balances -121,810.78; format_cents thousands opt-in, export.py CSV unchanged; only tally/money.py and report.py changed"
interlock assess add --criterion regression --strength tested --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "19 unit tests OK on this tree"
interlock check run --criterion balances; interlock check run --criterion regression; python3 -m tally settle examples/big.csv

interlock claim add --criterion balances --strength observed --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion balances" --note "check passed on output tree"
interlock claim add --criterion regression --strength tested --tree auto --ref "interlock check run --criterion regression" --note "19 unit tests pass"
interlock claim add --criterion spec --strength observed --tree auto --ref "python3 -m tally settle examples/big.csv" --note "settle prints 121,810.78; export still uses plain format_cents (default thousands=False)"
